audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gave Gragas level 3 where whys[2] says the trade is even, gave Skill at 4-5 and 6 where whys[3] says 'win every extended trade' and whys[4] calls it 'a genuine kill all-in', and gave Gragas at two-plus items where whys[6] says he runs you down.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Skill / Gragas / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill, matching the prose line for line. Win rate 54.07% over 344 games — you win the middle of the game and the late 1v1 flattens out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on either layer recorded the level 3 spike — Primal Howl coming online — even though it is the ability that most often breaks a Gragas combo.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second.' 15/14/13/12/11 second cooldown, 375 range.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[2], phases[2].why, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl's fear was absent everywhere, and the single most actionable interaction in this matchup was never stated: Infinite Duress 'leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed)' while Blood Hunt grants him move speed toward targets below 50% health — so the length of his ultimate leap is a function of your health bar. Staying above 50% keeps his R short and his passive healing off.
audit.why: Both halves are in Riot's own text: R 'scaling with his bonus Move Speed'; W 'senses enemies below 50% health, gaining Move Speed toward... when they fall below 25% health, he frenzies and these bonuses triple'; passive heals below 50%, tripling below 25%. Jaws of the Beast is 365 range, 8s at rank 1, deals damage based on max health and heals him.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull, dontsFull, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.why: Infinite Duress at 110s and Primal Howl at 15s are the timers that decide when you can commit.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both, plus what each actually does.

audit.why: Early Executioner's Calling is already core and is correct — his passive, Q and R all heal.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Use Explosive Cask' in the late paragraph — FALSE POSITIVE, the matcher caught the verb. All ability names in this matchup are correct. The content layer was already at the quality bar; the full layer was untouched boilerplate. The strongest previously-unstated fact, now written in, is that Infinite Duress's leap distance scales with bonus move speed while Blood Hunt only grants that speed against targets under 50% health — so your own health bar controls how far his ultimate reaches. Not asserted for lack of source: whether Tenacity, Cleanse or QSS affect the 1.5s suppression, and whether CC applied to Warwick mid-leap cancels it (the kit carries a 'channel' flag but Riot's text does not describe a channel, so the flag may be a parsing misfire).
